26	## Subagents
27	
28	Subagents are descriptor files at `.humanizephysics/subagents/<name>.md` (YAML frontmatter — `name`, `description`, `write_domain`, `read_only`, `can_spawn`, `default_enabled`, optional `mandatory: [<phase>...]`, optional `dispatcher_notes` — followed by the prompt body the spawned agent reads).
29	
30	**You do NOT need to discover subagents.** The plan and review prompts auto-inject an **Available subagents** section at the top of each invocation listing every enabled descriptor with description, write-domain, MANDATORY flag, and `dispatcher_notes`. When you decide to invoke a subagent, read its full prompt at `.humanizephysics/subagents/<name>.md`.
31	
32	**Invoke** via the generic wrapper (Bash tool, foreground):
33	
34	```
35	python3 .claude/tools/humanizephysics-subagent.py \
36	  --name <subagent-name> \
37	  --slug <kebab-slug> \
38	  --directive-file <path-to-directive.md> \
39	  --write-domain '<glob>'        # repeat for multiple
40	```
41	
42	The wrapper exits 0 on success, prints a one-line status, writes the report to `.humanizephysics/task_results/<name>-<slug>.md`, and the HumanizePhysics CLI auto-archives a copy to `logs/iter-NNN/<name>-<slug>-report.md` for the dashboard. The dispatch semaphore caps concurrent subagent processes at `loop.max_parallel`; the wrapper resolves `--parent-slug` from `HUMANIZEPHYSICS_SUBAGENT_SLUG` so nested children inherit the hierarchy.
43	
44	**A dispatch is a BLOCKING Bash call — wait by staying inside it.** `humanizephysics-subagent.py` is synchronous (it `subprocess.run`s the `humanizephysics subagent` CLI and returns only once the child finishes and its report is on disk). A long dispatch may be auto-backgrounded with a task ID — that's fine; wait for that task's result before acting. **Do NOT use the `Monitor` tool to wait** — it is non-blocking (returns immediately, "keep working"), so your turn ends and the subagents are abandoned mid-run. **Do NOT use foreground `sleep` / `until … ; do sleep … ; done`** — the harness blocks `sleep`. To run independent subagents **in parallel**, put all their dispatches in **one Bash call**, each backgrounded with `&`, ending with `wait` — e.g. `python3 .claude/tools/humanizephysics-subagent.py --name A … & python3 .claude/tools/humanizephysics-subagent.py --name B … & wait` — which blocks until all finish (the whole wave as one blocking dispatch). Serialize only subagents that write the **same file** (separate sequential calls). The rule never changes: do not consume a subagent's output until its report exists.
45	
46	**Highly-recommended subagents.** A descriptor whose frontmatter sets `mandatory: [plan]` is treated as **highly recommended** for the plan phase (similarly `[review]` for the review phase). The catalog tags them `[HIGHLY RECOMMENDED]`. Dispatch each one unless you have a concrete reason to skip — when skipping, record a one-line rationale under a `## Subagent skips` section in `iter/iter-NNN/<phase>.md` (e.g. `- strategy-critic: STRATEGY.md SHA unchanged from prior iter and last verdict was SOUND`). A post-phase audit checks both signals: it silences when the subagent dispatched OR a skip rationale was recorded, and warns only when neither happened. Each subagent's `dispatcher_notes` enumerates its specific skip conditions — read them before deciding. **Subagents ship disabled by default** (`default_enabled: false`), so the rule only fires for subagents the user has explicitly listed under `subagents.enabled` in `.humanizephysics/config.json`; on a fresh project the catalog is empty and no recommended dispatch is required.

92	## Blueprint Marker Vocabulary
93	
94	Two semantic markers:
95	
96	- `\leanok` — statement block: declaration is formalized (at least a `sorry` present). Proof block: proof closed, no `sorry`.
97	- `\mathlibok` — statement block: declaration is backed by Mathlib (re-export / alias); no HumanizePhysics proof obligation remains.
98	
99	No marker means the block is unformalized. If a block fails to translate, leave it unmarked and annotate with a `% NOTE:` comment.
100	
101	**`\leanok` is managed deterministically by the `sync_leanok` phase** that runs between prover and review each iteration. It walks every chapter, looks up each `\lean{...}` declaration, runs `sorry_analyzer` + `lake build <module>` (it uses `lake build`, not `lake env lean <file>`, so dependencies are built and missing-import failures aren't spurious), and adds/removes `\leanok` accordingly. Agents should NOT add or remove `\leanok` as routine bookkeeping — leave it to the sync. The one exception is the review agent: if it is **certain** the sync got a marker wrong (a clearly-finished proof left unmarked, or a marker present on something incomplete), it may manually correct it, but must explicitly surface and justify that override in its summary (see `.humanizephysics/prompts/review.md`).
102	
103	`\mathlibok`, `\lean{...}` corrections, and `% NOTE:` annotations are the review agent's domain (they require semantic judgement). The plan agent writes informal prose and `\lean{...}` hints; provers never touch the blueprint.

105	## User Interaction
106	
107	The user provides hints in two places:
108	
109	- **Strategic hints** → `.humanizephysics/USER_HINTS.md`. The HumanizePhysics loop captures this file's content before each plan phase, injects it into the plan agent's prompt, and resets the file to its bundled template (an HTML-comment format guide + zero bullets) after the plan phase succeeds. The HTML-comment preamble is stripped before injection so a template-only file renders as "no hints" to the planner. The plan agent does NOT read or clear that file itself. 111	
112	HumanizePhysics talks back to the user through **`TO_USER.md`** — a single, *persistent* notice board surfaced as a UI banner. It is **shared and writable by every agent** (plan, prover, review). It is no longer cleared at the start of each review phase; content survives across iters until an agent prunes it. The discipline every writer follows:
113	
114	- **Concise**: the whole file stays ≤ 2–3 short bullets. It is a banner, not a log.
115	- **Relevant now**: before adding anything, read the current content and **delete any bullet that is no longer true or important at this point** (the blocker was resolved, the decision was overtaken, the credential got set). Never let it accumulate stale notices.
116	- **Notice board, never a question queue**: the loop is autonomous and may run unattended for many iters. Never write "awaiting your decision", an options menu, a "where to reply", or "default to X if no reply" — anything implying the loop is paused for a human. State decisions as *made* and blockers as *worked-around-as-far-as-possible*; the user steers asynchronously via `USER_HINTS.md`.

15	  `O₂` fragment has mass `2m`; the photon momentum is `p_γ = E_γ/c = ℏω/c`.
16	
17	  Current subquestion (T1-C1, 2.5 pts):
18	    Determine the minimum angular frequency `ω_min` required for the
19	    dissociation to occur at outgoing `O₂` angle `θ`, in terms of
20	    `ℏ, c, θ, ΔU` and `m`.
21	
22	  Recorded official answer:
23	    for `θ ≤ π/2`,
24	      `ω_min = 3 m c² (1 - √(1 - (2 ΔU / (3 m c²)) (2 sin²θ + 1))) /
25	                 (ℏ (2 sin²θ + 1))`;
26	    for `θ ≥ π/2`, the same threshold evaluated at `θ = π/2`.
27	  (Official solution, `T1_solution.txt`: the threshold is the smallest root of
28	  `(cos 2θ - 2) ℏ²ω² + 6 m c² ℏω - 6 ΔU m c² = 0`, and
29	  `2 sin²θ + 1 = 2 - cos 2θ`.)
30	
31	  All theorem statements below are faithful contracts.  The current target
32	  conclusion — the closed-form value of `ω_min` — appears only on the
33	  conclusion side of the main theorems `minimum_angular_frequency_T1_C1` /
34	  `minimum_angular_frequency_backward_branch_T1_C1` and of the auxiliary
35	  quadratic-form lemma `quadratic_characterization_of_threshold`; the
36	  governing-law predicates (`IsTwoBodyDissociation`, `IsScatteringAngle`)
37	  never mention it.
38	
39	  Iter-017 redraft (proof-Review certificate `needs_redraft`,
40	  other_modeling_defect): the official solution attains the threshold at the
41	  degenerate critical configuration `p = 0` (the `O₂` fragment at rest, the
42	  `O` atom carrying the full photon momentum) for every `θ ≥ π/2`, including
43	  the forward theorem's boundary `θ = π/2` — the tangent point of the
44	  velocity circle at `θ = 90°` is the origin, and for larger angles the
45	  threshold circle passes through the origin (`T1_solution.txt`, T1-C1).
46	  Accordingly `IsScatteringAngle` no longer excludes `p = 0`, and the
47	  backward theorem's discriminant hypothesis is the real-square-root
48	  condition at `π/2`, `0 ≤ 1 − 2ΔU/(mc²)`; the earlier
49	  `0 ≤ 1 − 2ΔU/(3mc²)` admitted the regime `ΔU ∈ (mc²/2, 3mc²/2]`, where
50	  nothing at all is reachable at backward angles.  The two reachability
51	  conjuncts remain `sorry` (proof-lane work); every other proof in the file —
52	  in particular both minimality conjuncts — is unchanged and never used the
53	  dropped `p ≠ 0`.
54	-/

107	section ReactionGeometry
108	
109	/-!
110	Geometry of the reaction (Figure 1c).  The incoming photon and the two
111	outgoing fragments are coplanar; the `O₂` momentum `p⃗` makes the angle `θ`
112	with the incident photon direction.  Vectors live in an abstract Euclidean
113	2-space so that the momentum-conservation law is a genuine vector equation.
114	-/
115	
116	/-- The plane containing the incident photon and the outgoing fragments in
117	    Figure 1c: a two-dimensional Euclidean space.  Using an abstract inner
118	    product space (rather than coordinate pairs of reals) keeps the notion of
119	    *angle between momentum vectors* intrinsic. -/
120	abbrev ReactionPlane : Type := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)
121	
122	/-- The direction of the incident photon (and of its momentum) in the
123	    reaction plane: a unit vector. -/
124	structure PhotonLine where
125	  direction : ReactionPlane
126	  direction_unit : ‖direction‖ = 1
127	
128	/-- `θ` is the angle between the outgoing `O₂` momentum `p` and the incident
129	    photon direction `k̂`, as read from Figure 1c: the cosine-law component
130	    statement `⟪k̂, p⟫ = ‖p‖ * cos θ`.
131	
132	    For `p ≠ 0` this is exactly the statement that `θ` is the angle between
133	    the two momentum vectors.  The degenerate case `p = 0` — the `O₂`
134	    fragment produced at rest, with the `O` atom carrying the full photon
135	    momentum — is admitted: the cosine law is then vacuous (`0 = 0`) at every
136	    `θ`.  This matches the official solution (`T1_solution.txt`, T1-C1): the
137	    tangent critical configuration at `θ = 90°` is the origin point of the
138	    velocity circle, and for `θ ≥ 90°` the threshold circle passes through
139	    the origin, so the official answer counts the threshold as *attained* at
140	    `p = 0`.  Excluding `p = 0` would make the threshold an unattained
141	    infimum and both main theorems below false (proof-Review certificate,
142	    iter-017). -/
143	def IsScatteringAngle (k : PhotonLine) (p : ReactionPlane) (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
144	  @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction p = ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ
145	
146	/-- The angular range of the problem: `θ ∈ [0, π]`.  The branch information
147	    (`θ ≤ π/2` versus `θ ≥ π/2`) is preserved by hypothesis, not selected
148	    only in the conclusion. -/
149	def IsAngularRange (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
150	  θ ∈ Icc 0 Real.pi
151	
152	/-- The forward / non-backscattering branch of the official solution:
153	    `θ ≤ π/2`.  The official solution warns that the tangent-line critical
154	    configuration of Figure 1c exists only in this branch; for `θ ≥ π/2` the
155	    threshold freezes at its `θ = π/2` value. -/
156	def IsForwardBranch (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
157	  θ ≤ Real.pi / 2
158	
159	end ReactionGeometry

161	section GoverningLaws
162	
163	/-!
164	Governing physical laws.  These predicates state the modelling relations
165	directly (photon momentum `p_γ = ℏω/c`, vector momentum conservation with
166	the Figure-1c angle readout, and non-relativistic energy balance with
167	fragment masses `2m` and `m`).  None of them mentions the closed-form
168	threshold that the current subquestion asks to determine.
169	-/
170	
171	/-- Lawful configurations of the absorption + two-body breakup
172	    `γ + O₃ → O₂ + O` in Figure 1c.  Every field is a constraining equation
173	    that a later proof can rewrite with:
174	
175	    * `momentum_q_sq` — vector momentum conservation `ℏω/c · k̂ = p⃗ + q⃗`,
176	      eliminated to the cosine-law component statement
177	      `‖q‖² = (ℏω/c)² + ‖p‖² − 2 (ℏω/c) ‖p‖ cos θ`;
178	    * `q_unique` — the vector equation determines `q` uniquely as
179	      `q = (ℏω/c) • k̂ − p`;
180	    * `angle_readout` — the Figure-1c readout that `θ` is the angle between
181	      `p⃗` and the incident photon direction;
182	    * `energy_balance` — non-relativistic energy conservation
183	      `ℏω = ΔU + ‖p‖²/(2·2m) + ‖q‖²/(2m)`.
184	
185	    None of the fields quantifies over configurations or mentions the
186	    minimum; those appear only on the conclusion side of the theorems below. -/
187	structure IsTwoBodyDissociation
188	    (k : PhotonLine) (ω θ m dU : ℝ) (p q : ReactionPlane) : Prop where
189	  /-- Cosine-law magnitude equation from `ℏω/c · k̂ = p⃗ + q⃗`:
190	      `‖q‖² = (ℏω/c)² + ‖p‖² − 2 (ℏω/c) ‖p‖ cos θ`. -/
191	  momentum_q_sq :
192	    ‖q‖ ^ 2 = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) ^ 2 + ‖p‖ ^ 2
193	      - 2 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ
194	  /-- The vector momentum balance determines the `O` momentum uniquely as
195	      `q = (ℏω/c) • k̂ − p`. -/
196	  q_unique : q = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) • k.direction - p
197	  /-- Figure-1c angle readout between the photon direction and `p`. -/
198	  angle_readout : IsScatteringAngle k p θ
199	  /-- Non-relativistic energy balance: the photon energy `ℏω` covers the
200	      dissociation gap `ΔU` plus the classical kinetic energies of the `O₂`
201	      fragment (mass `2m`) and the `O` fragment (mass `m`). -/
202	  energy_balance :
203	    hbar * ω = dU + ‖p‖ ^ 2 / (2 * (2 * m)) + ‖q‖ ^ 2 / (2 * m)
204	
205	/-- Elimination/bridge lemma: the cosine-law component equation is a genuine
206	    consequence of the vector momentum balance and the angle readout, so the
207	    `momentum_q_sq` field is the eliminated shadow of `q_unique` rather than
208	    an independent modelling assumption.  Recording this implication is what
209	    makes the interface constraining: any countermodel must satisfy a vector
210	    equation, not just an isolated scalar identity. -/
211	theorem momentum_q_sq_of_vector_balance
212	    (k : PhotonLine) (ω θ : ℝ) (p q : ReactionPlane)
213	    (hq : q = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) • k.direction - p)
214	    (hθ : IsScatteringAngle k p θ) :
215	    ‖q‖ ^ 2 = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) ^ 2 + ‖p‖ ^ 2
216	      - 2 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := by
217	  have hinner : @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction p = ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := hθ
218	  set a : ℝ := hbar * ω / speedOfLight with ha
219	  have hk : @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction k.direction = 1 := by
220	    rw [@inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, k.direction_unit]
221	    norm_num
222	  have hsq : ‖q‖ ^ 2 = @inner ℝ _ _ q q := by
223	    rw [@inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K]
224	    norm_num
225	  calc ‖q‖ ^ 2 = @inner ℝ _ _ q q := hsq
226	    _ = @inner ℝ _ _ (a • k.direction) (a • k.direction)
227	          - 2 * @inner ℝ _ _ (a • k.direction) p + @inner ℝ _ _ p p := by
228	          rw [hq, real_inner_sub_sub_self]
229	    _ = a ^ 2 * @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction k.direction
230	          - 2 * a * @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction p + @inner ℝ _ _ p p := by
231	          rw [@real_inner_smul_left, @real_inner_smul_left,
232	            @real_inner_smul_right]
233	          ring
234	    _ = a ^ 2 + ‖p‖ ^ 2 - 2 * a * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := by
235	          rw [hk, hinner, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
236	          ring
237	    _ = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) ^ 2 + ‖p‖ ^ 2
238	          - 2 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := by
239	          rw [ha]
240	
241	end GoverningLaws

243	section ThresholdContracts
244	
245	/-!
246	Reachable frequencies and the threshold contracts.  The recorded closed-form
247	value of `ω_min` occurs ONLY on the conclusion side of the main theorems
248	below: `ReachableFrequency` and `IsDissociationThreshold` are pure
249	minimality statements over lawful configurations, and the candidate formula
250	`hbarOmegaMin` is a bare scalar expression that, by itself, asserts nothing
251	about dissociation.  The main theorem `minimum_angular_frequency_T1_C1`
252	bridges the two.
253	-/
254	
255	/-- `ω` is reachable at outgoing `O₂` angle `θ` (with oxygen-atom mass `m`
256	    and dissociation gap `dU`) iff some lawful dissociation configuration
257	    realizes that photon frequency.  This is a physical reachability
258	    statement — an existential over geometry and fragment momenta — not a
259	    formula.  Following the official solution, the degenerate threshold
260	    configuration `p = 0` (the `O₂` fragment at rest) counts as a
261	    configuration at every angle; see `IsScatteringAngle`. -/
262	def ReachableFrequency (m dU θ ω : ℝ) : Prop :=
263	  ∃ (k : PhotonLine) (p q : ReactionPlane), IsTwoBodyDissociation k ω θ m dU p q
264	
265	/-- `ω₀` is *a* dissociation threshold at angle `θ` iff it is reachable and
266	    no strictly smaller positive frequency is reachable.  This is a
267	    minimality property over `ReachableFrequency`; the numerical value of
268	    the threshold is left completely open. -/
269	def IsDissociationThreshold (m dU θ ω₀ : ℝ) : Prop :=
270	  ReachableFrequency m dU θ ω₀ ∧
271	    ∀ ω : ℝ, 0 < ω → ω < ω₀ → ¬ ReachableFrequency m dU θ ω
272	
273	/-- The candidate closed-form forward-branch threshold, in terms of the
274	    oxygen-atom mass `m`, the speed of light `c`, the dissociation gap `ΔU`,
275	    and the scattering angle `θ`:
276	
277	    `Ω(m, c, ΔU, θ) = 3 m c² (1 − √(1 − (2 ΔU/(3 m c²)) (2 sin²θ + 1)))
278	                      / (ℏ (2 sin²θ + 1))`.
279	
280	    This is only a bare real-valued expression — the recorded official
281	    answer.  By itself it asserts nothing about the dissociation; the
282	    physical claim that it *is* the minimum reachable frequency is exactly
283	    the content of `minimum_angular_frequency_T1_C1` below.  The official
284	    solution also notes `2 sin²θ + 1 = 2 − cos 2θ`, and that the same value
285	    is the smallest positive root of
286	    `(2 − cos 2θ)(ℏω)² − 6 m c² (ℏω) + 6 ΔU m c² = 0`. -/
287	def hbarOmegaMin (m c dU θ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
288	  3 * m * c ^ 2 * (1 - Real.sqrt (1 - (2 * dU / (3 * m * c ^ 2)) * (2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 + 1))) /
289	    (hbar * (2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 + 1))
290	
291	/-- Trigonometric helper from the official solution: the angular factor of
292	    the threshold formula equals `2 − cos 2θ`.  Pure Mathlib content,
293	    isolated so that both the quadratic-root form and the displayed
294	    `ω_min` form of the answer can share it. -/
295	theorem two_sin_sq_add_one_eq (θ : ℝ) :
296	    2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 + 1 = 2 - Real.cos (2 * θ) := by
297	  have h : Real.cos (2 * θ) = 2 * Real.cos θ ^ 2 - 1 := Real.cos_two_mul θ
298	  have h' := Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq θ
299	  linarith
300	
301	/-- Quadratic characterization of the candidate threshold (official
302	    solution): in the positive regime (including `ℏ > 0`, needed since the
303	    candidate `Ω` carries a `1/ℏ` factor), for forward angles and a
304	    nondegenerate angular factor, `E₀ = ℏ · Ω(m, c, ΔU, θ)` is the smallest
305	    positive root of
306	    `(2 − cos 2θ) E² − 6 m c² E + 6 ΔU m c² = 0`.  Stating the equivalence
307	    here (rather than only the displayed closed form) keeps the official
308	    derivation route — minimization of the energy/momentum balance reduces to
309	    this quadratic — available to later proof steps. -/
310	theorem quadratic_characterization_of_threshold
311	    (m c dU θ : ℝ)
312	    (hm : 0 < m) (hc : 0 < c) (hdU : 0 < dU) (hb : 0 < hbar)
313	    (hθ : IsForwardBranch θ) (hθpos : 0 < θ)
314	    (hfac : (2:ℝ) - Real.cos (2 * θ) ≠ 0)
315	    (hdisc : 0 ≤ 1 - (2 * dU / (3 * m * c ^ 2)) * (2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 + 1)) :
316	    let E₀ := hbar * hbarOmegaMin m c dU θ
317	    0 < E₀ ∧
318	      (2 - Real.cos (2 * θ)) * E₀ ^ 2 - 6 * m * c ^ 2 * E₀ + 6 * dU * m * c ^ 2 = 0 ∧
319	      ∀ E : ℝ, 0 < E →
320	        (2 - Real.cos (2 * θ)) * E ^ 2 - 6 * m * c ^ 2 * E + 6 * dU * m * c ^ 2 = 0 →
321	        E₀ ≤ E := by
322	  show 0 < hbar * hbarOmegaMin m c dU θ ∧ _ ∧ _
323	  have hmc : (0:ℝ) < 3 * m * c ^ 2 := by positivity
324	  have hmcne : (3:ℝ) * m * c ^ 2 ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hmc
325	  set S : ℝ := 2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 + 1 with hSdef
326	  have hS : (1:ℝ) ≤ S := by
327	    rw [hSdef]
328	    have hss := sq_nonneg (Real.sin θ)
329	    linarith
330	  have hSpos : (0:ℝ) < S := lt_of_lt_of_le one_pos hS
331	  have hSne : S ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hSpos
332	  set D : ℝ := 1 - (2 * dU / (3 * m * c ^ 2)) * S with hDdef
333	  set s : ℝ := Real.sqrt D with hsdef
334	  have hs_nonneg : 0 ≤ s := Real.sqrt_nonneg D
335	  have hs_sq : s ^ 2 = D := Real.sq_sqrt hdisc
336	  have hfracS : (2 * dU / (3 * m * c ^ 2)) * (3 * m * c ^ 2) = 2 * dU := by
337	    field_simp [hmcne]
338	  have hsq3 : s ^ 2 * (3 * m * c ^ 2) = 3 * m * c ^ 2 - 2 * dU * S := by
339	    linear_combination (3 * m * c ^ 2) * hs_sq - S * hfracS
340	  have hfrac : (0:ℝ) < 2 * dU / (3 * m * c ^ 2) := by positivity
341	  have hDlt : (0:ℝ) < 1 - D := by
342	    have hmul : (0:ℝ) < (2 * dU / (3 * m * c ^ 2)) * S := mul_pos hfrac hSpos
343	    rw [hDdef]
344	    linarith
345	  have hsq_lt : s ^ 2 < (1:ℝ) ^ 2 := by
346	    rw [hs_sq]
347	    linarith [hDlt]
348	  have hs_lt_one : s < 1 := by
349	    have h1 := abs_lt_of_sq_lt_sq hsq_lt (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1)
350	    exact (abs_lt.mp h1).2
351	  have hone_sub : (0:ℝ) < 1 - s := by linarith
352	  have hfac_S : (2:ℝ) - Real.cos (2 * θ) = S := (two_sin_sq_add_one_eq θ).symm
353	  set X : ℝ := 3 * m * c ^ 2 * (1 - s) with hXdef
354	  have hΩ : hbarOmegaMin m c dU θ = X / (hbar * S) := rfl
355	  have hE : hbar * hbarOmegaMin m c dU θ = X / S := by
356	    rw [hΩ]
357	    have hbne : hbar ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hb
358	    have hden : hbar * S ≠ 0 := mul_ne_zero hbne hSne
359	    field_simp
360	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
361	  · rw [hE]
362	    exact div_pos (mul_pos hmc hone_sub) hSpos
363	  · rw [hfac_S, hE]
364	    have hS2ne : (S:ℝ) ^ 2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hSne
365	    have h1 : S ^ 2 * (X / S) ^ 2 = X ^ 2 := by
366	      rw [div_pow, ← mul_div_assoc]
367	      exact mul_div_cancel_left₀ (X ^ 2) hS2ne
368	    have h2 : (X / S) * S = X := div_mul_cancel₀ X hSne
369	    have key : (S * (X / S) ^ 2 - 6 * m * c ^ 2 * (X / S) + 6 * dU * m * c ^ 2) * S ^ 2
370	        = S * X ^ 2 - 6 * m * c ^ 2 * S * X + 6 * dU * m * c ^ 2 * S ^ 2 := by
371	      linear_combination S * h1 - 6 * m * c ^ 2 * S * h2
372	    have hroot : S * X ^ 2 - 6 * m * c ^ 2 * S * X + 6 * dU * m * c ^ 2 * S ^ 2 = 0 := by
373	      rw [hXdef]
374	      linear_combination (S * (3 * m * c ^ 2)) * hsq3
375	    have hprod : (S * (X / S) ^ 2 - 6 * m * c ^ 2 * (X / S) + 6 * dU * m * c ^ 2) * S ^ 2
376	        = 0 := by rw [key]; exact hroot
377	    rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hprod with h | h'
378	    · exact h
379	    · exact absurd h' hS2ne
380	  · intro E _hEpos hEroot
381	    rw [hfac_S] at hEroot
382	    have hfactor :
383	        (S * E - 3 * m * c ^ 2 * (1 - s)) * (S * E - 3 * m * c ^ 2 * (1 + s)) = 0 := by
384	      linear_combination S * hEroot - (3 * m * c ^ 2) * hsq3
385	    rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hfactor with h1 | h2
386	    · have hE1 : E = 3 * m * c ^ 2 * (1 - s) / S := by
387	        rw [eq_div_iff hSne]
388	        linarith
389	      rw [hE, hE1]
390	    · have hE2 : E = 3 * m * c ^ 2 * (1 + s) / S := by
391	        rw [eq_div_iff hSne]
392	        linarith
393	      rw [hE, hE2]
394	      have hB : 3 * m * c ^ 2 * (1 - s) ≤ 3 * m * c ^ 2 * (1 + s) := by nlinarith
395	      exact (div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hSpos).mpr hB
396	
397	
398	/-- **Bridge: the momentum-magnitude quadratic.**  From the fields of any lawful
399	    dissociation configuration, `P = ‖p‖` is a real root of the
400	    official-solution quadratic `3P² − 4a cosθ·P + (2a² + 4mΔU − 4mE) = 0`
401	    with `a = ℏω/c`, `E = ℏω`.  Pure field algebra from the structure fields;
402	    no threshold value is used. -/
403	theorem config_quadratic
404	    (k : PhotonLine) (ω θ m dU : ℝ) (p q : ReactionPlane) (hm : 0 < m)
405	    (h : IsTwoBodyDissociation k ω θ m dU p q) :
406	    3 * ‖p‖ ^ 2 - 4 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) * Real.cos θ * ‖p‖
407	      + (2 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) ^ 2 + 4 * m * dU - 4 * m * (hbar * ω)) = 0 := by
408	  obtain ⟨hq_sq, _hq_uniq, _hangle, henb⟩ := h
409	  have hm2 : (2:ℝ) * m ≠ 0 := by positivity
410	  have hm4 : (2:ℝ) * (2 * m) ≠ 0 := by positivity
411	  rw [hq_sq] at henb
412	  field_simp [hm2, hm4] at henb
413	  linear_combination -henb
414	
415	/-- **Recoil sign at non-forward angles.**  At any angle with `cos θ ≤ 0`, every
416	    lawful configuration has `C(E) ≤ 0`, where `C(E) = 2(E/c)² + 4mΔU − 4mE`:
417	    the momentum quadratic rewrites as `C = −3P² + 4aPcosθ`, and both terms are
418	    nonpositive when `cos θ ≤ 0`.  The proof uses only the cosine-law half of

72	### Subagent permissions
73	
74	Each subagent ships YAML frontmatter:
75	
76	- `write_domain: "<glob>"` — file pattern the subagent may write. Empty for purely read-only subagents (the dispatching call typically passes `--write-domain 'task_results/**'` so the subagent can still write its own report).
77	- `read_only: true | false` — when `true`, the subagent may only write its `task_results/<name>-<slug>.md`.
78	- `can_spawn: true | false` — when `true`, the subagent may dispatch children whose `write_domain` is a subset of its own.
79	
80	The dispatcher enforces `write_domain` at the filesystem level: any child whose declared domain is not a subset of the parent's is rejected before the child agent starts. Reads are restricted only by the descriptor's prompt body (e.g. fresh-context critics that are told not to read PROGRESS.md / STRATEGY.md).
81	
82	**`.humanizephysics/REFACTOR_DIRECTIVE.md`** is reserved for the interactive `humanizephysics refactor draft` / `humanizephysics refactor run` flow run by hand by the mathematician. The autonomous loop never reads or writes that file. To invoke a refactor-style subagent inside the loop, write the directive to a fresh tempfile under `.humanizephysics/logs/iter-NNN/<name>-<slug>-directive.md` and dispatch via the generic wrapper.
83	
84	## Protected Declarations
85	
86	`humanizephysics-protected.yaml` at the project root lists declarations whose **signatures are frozen** by the mathematician. Rules:
87	
88	- **Plan / prover / review** agents: read-only on protected signatures. May fill proof bodies; may not rename, re-type, or reorder arguments.
89	- **Write-capable structural subagents** (per their `write_domain`): may *move* a protected declaration to a different file (name + signature preserved verbatim) and must then update the path key in `humanizephysics-protected.yaml`. They may NEVER rename / re-type / delete / re-sign a protected declaration.
90	- The YAML file itself is user-only. No agent adds or removes a declaration. The only allowed agent edit is updating an existing declaration's file path.
91	
92	## Blueprint Marker Vocabulary
93	
94	Two semantic markers:
95	
96	- `\leanok` — statement block: declaration is formalized (at least a `sorry` present). Proof block: proof closed, no `sorry`.
97	- `\mathlibok` — statement block: declaration is backed by Mathlib (re-export / alias); no HumanizePhysics proof obligation remains.
98	
99	No marker means the block is unformalized. If a block fails to translate, leave it unmarked and annotate with a `% NOTE:` comment.
100	
101	**`\leanok` is managed deterministically by the `sync_leanok` phase** that runs between prover and review each iteration. It walks every chapter, looks up each `\lean{...}` declaration, runs `sorry_analyzer` + `lake build <module>` (it uses `lake build`, not `lake env lean <file>`, so dependencies are built and missing-import failures aren't spurious), and adds/removes `\leanok` accordingly. Agents should NOT add or remove `\leanok` as routine bookkeeping — leave it to the sync. The one exception is the review agent: if it is **certain** the sync got a marker wrong (a clearly-finished proof left unmarked, or a marker present on something incomplete), it may manually correct it, but must explicitly surface and justify that override in its summary (see `.humanizephysics/prompts/review.md`).
102	
103	`\mathlibok`, `\lean{...}` corrections, and `% NOTE:` annotations are the review agent's domain (they require semantic judgement). The plan agent writes informal prose and `\lean{...}` hints; provers never touch the blueprint.
104	
105	## User Interaction
106	
107	The user provides hints in two places:
108	
109	- **Strategic hints** → `.humanizephysics/USER_HINTS.md`. The HumanizePhysics loop captures this file's content before each plan phase, injects it into the plan agent's prompt, and resets the file to its bundled template (an HTML-comment format guide + zero bullets) after the plan phase succeeds. The HTML-comment preamble is stripped before injection so a template-only file renders as "no hints" to the planner. The plan agent does NOT read or clear that file itself. Provers never see these hints.
110	- **File-specific hints** → `/- USER: ... -/` comments directly in `.lean` files. The prover that owns that file sees them naturally.
111	
112	HumanizePhysics talks back to the user through **`TO_USER.md`** — a single, *persistent* notice board surfaced as a UI banner. It is **shared and writable by every agent** (plan, prover, review). It is no longer cleared at the start of each review phase; content survives across iters until an agent prunes it. The discipline every writer follows:
113	
114	- **Concise**: the whole file stays ≤ 2–3 short bullets. It is a banner, not a log.
115	- **Relevant now**: before adding anything, read the current content and **delete any bullet that is no longer true or important at this point** (the blocker was resolved, the decision was overtaken, the credential got set). Never let it accumulate stale notices.
116	- **Notice board, never a question queue**: the loop is autonomous and may run unattended for many iters. Never write "awaiting your decision", an options menu, a "where to reply", or "default to X if no reply" — anything implying the loop is paused for a human. State decisions as *made* and blockers as *worked-around-as-far-as-possible*; the user steers asynchronously via `USER_HINTS.md`.
117

Keep only durable facts that would surprise an agent reading the code fresh (dead-end tactics, files not to touch, Mathlib gap coordinates, protected invariants). Hard limits: ~10 bullets / ~600 chars; prune before adding. Do NOT duplicate what's obvious from the code or PROGRESS.md.
128	- Write informal prose in `blueprint/src/chapters/*.tex`. Do NOT touch markers — `\leanok` is owned by the deterministic sync; `\mathlibok` / `% NOTE:` by the review agent.

3	
4	  Blueprint chapter: blueprint/src/chapters/IPhO2026Problems_problem_IPhO_2026_1_C_1.tex

8	  Physical situation (Figure 1c):
9	  A photon of angular frequency `ω` strikes an ozone molecule `O₃` at rest and
10	  is absorbed, dissociating it into an oxygen molecule `O₂` and an oxygen atom
11	  `O`.  The ground-state energies of `O₃` and of the fragments are `Uᵢ` and
12	  `U_f`, with `ΔU = U_f - Uᵢ > 0`.  The momentum of the outgoing `O₂` makes
13	  the angle `θ` with the incident photon direction.  The fragments are treated
14	  classically and non-relativistically; an oxygen atom has mass `m`, so the
15	  `O₂` fragment has mass `2m`; the photon momentum is `p_γ = E_γ/c = ℏω/c`.
16	
17	  Current subquestion (T1-C1, 2.5 pts):
18	    Determine the minimum angular frequency `ω_min` required for the
19	    dissociation to occur at outgoing `O₂` angle `θ`, in terms of
20	    `ℏ, c, θ, ΔU` and `m`.
21	
22	  Recorded official answer:
23	    for `θ ≤ π/2`,
24	      `ω_min = 3 m c² (1 - √(1 - (2 ΔU / (3 m c²)) (2 sin²θ + 1))) /
25	                 (ℏ (2 sin²θ + 1))`;
26	    for `θ ≥ π/2`, the same threshold evaluated at `θ = π/2`.
27	  (Official solution, `T1_solution.txt`: the threshold is the smallest root of
28	  `(cos 2θ - 2) ℏ²ω² + 6 m c² ℏω - 6 ΔU m c² = 0`, and
29	  `2 sin²θ + 1 = 2 - cos 2θ`.)
30	
31	  All theorem statements below are faithful contracts.  The current target
32	  conclusion — the closed-form value of `ω_min` — appears only on the
33	  conclusion side of the main theorems `minimum_angular_frequency_T1_C1` /
34	  `minimum_angular_frequency_backward_branch_T1_C1` and of the auxiliary
35	  quadratic-form lemma `quadratic_characterization_of_threshold`; the
36	  governing-law predicates (`IsTwoBodyDissociation`, `IsScatteringAngle`)
37	  never mention it.
38

40	  other_modeling_defect): the official solution attains the threshold at the

62	namespace IPhO2026.Problem1.C1
63	
64	section UniversalConstants
65	
66	/-!
67	Universal constants and molecular data of the problem.  They are declared as
68	abstract scalars (with their SI roles recorded in the docstrings) rather than
69	transparent aliases, so that the contracts below cannot be closed by
70	unfolding.
71	-/
72	
73	/-- Reduced Planck constant `ℏ` (J·s). -/
74	opaque hbar : ℝ
75	
76	/-- Speed of light in vacuum `c` (m/s). -/
77	opaque speedOfLight : ℝ
78	
79	/-- Mass `m` of one oxygen atom (kg); the `O₂` fragment has mass `2m`. -/
80	opaque oxygenAtomMass : ℝ
81	
82	/-- Photon angular frequency `ω` for any photon considered in this process
83	    (rad/s).  The closed-form value of `ω_min` is a *target*, not a datum. -/
84	opaque photonAngularFrequency : ℝ
85	
86	/-- Ground-state energy `Uᵢ` of the ozone molecule `O₃` (J). -/
87	opaque ozoneGroundStateEnergy : ℝ
88	
89	/-- Ground-state energy `U_f` of the photofragments `O₂ + O` (J). -/
90	opaque fragmentsGroundStateEnergy : ℝ
91	
92	/-- Energy gap `ΔU = U_f − Uᵢ` (J): the energy that must be supplied to
93	    dissociate ozone at rest into `O₂ + O`. -/
94	def dissociationEnergyGap : ℝ :=
95	  fragmentsGroundStateEnergy - ozoneGroundStateEnergy
96	
97	/-- Positivity of the universal constants (physical regime of the problem). -/
98	structure ConstantRegime : Prop where
99	  hbar_pos : 0 < hbar
100	  speedOfLight_pos : 0 < speedOfLight
101	  oxygenAtomMass_pos : 0 < oxygenAtomMass
102	  /-- The dissociation is endothermic: `ΔU > 0`. -/
103	  gap_pos : 0 < dissociationEnergyGap
104	
105	end UniversalConstants

107	section ReactionGeometry
108	
109	/-!
110	Geometry of the reaction (Figure 1c).  The incoming photon and the two
111	outgoing fragments are coplanar; the `O₂` momentum `p⃗` makes the angle `θ`
112	with the incident photon direction.  Vectors live in an abstract Euclidean
113	2-space so that the momentum-conservation law is a genuine vector equation.
114	-/
115	
116	/-- The plane containing the incident photon and the outgoing fragments in
117	    Figure 1c: a two-dimensional Euclidean space.  Using an abstract inner
118	    product space (rather than coordinate pairs of reals) keeps the notion of
119	    *angle between momentum vectors* intrinsic. -/
120	abbrev ReactionPlane : Type := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)
121	
122	/-- The direction of the incident photon (and of its momentum) in the
123	    reaction plane: a unit vector. -/
124	structure PhotonLine where
125	  direction : ReactionPlane
126	  direction_unit : ‖direction‖ = 1
127	
128	/-- `θ` is the angle between the outgoing `O₂` momentum `p` and the incident
129	    photon direction `k̂`, as read from Figure 1c: the cosine-law component
130	    statement `⟪k̂, p⟫ = ‖p‖ * cos θ`.
131	
132	    For `p ≠ 0` this is exactly the statement that `θ` is the angle between
133	    the two momentum vectors.  The degenerate case `p = 0` — the `O₂`
134	    fragment produced at rest, with the `O` atom carrying the full photon
135	    momentum — is admitted: the cosine law is then vacuous (`0 = 0`) at every
136	    `θ`.  This matches the official solution (`T1_solution.txt`, T1-C1): the
137	    tangent critical configuration at `θ = 90°` is the origin point of the
138	    velocity circle, and for `θ ≥ 90°` the threshold circle passes through
139	    the origin, so the official answer counts the threshold as *attained* at
140	    `p = 0`.  Excluding `p = 0` would make the threshold an unattained
141	    infimum and both main theorems below false (proof-Review certificate,
142	    iter-017). -/
143	def IsScatteringAngle (k : PhotonLine) (p : ReactionPlane) (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
144	  @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction p = ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ
145	
146	/-- The angular range of the problem: `θ ∈ [0, π]`.  The branch information
147	    (`θ ≤ π/2` versus `θ ≥ π/2`) is preserved by hypothesis, not selected
148	    only in the conclusion. -/
149	def IsAngularRange (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
150	  θ ∈ Icc 0 Real.pi

152	/-- The forward / non-backscattering branch of the official solution:
153	    `θ ≤ π/2`.  The official solution warns that the tangent-line critical
154	    configuration of Figure 1c exists only in this branch; for `θ ≥ π/2` the
155	    threshold freezes at its `θ = π/2` value. -/
156	def IsForwardBranch (θ : ℝ) : Prop :=
157	  θ ≤ Real.pi / 2

162	
163	/-!
164	Governing physical laws.  These predicates state the modelling relations
165	directly (photon momentum `p_γ = ℏω/c`, vector momentum conservation with
166	the Figure-1c angle readout, and non-relativistic energy balance with
167	fragment masses `2m` and `m`).  None of them mentions the closed-form
168	threshold that the current subquestion asks to determine.
169	-/
170	
171	/-- Lawful configurations of the absorption + two-body breakup
172	    `γ + O₃ → O₂ + O` in Figure 1c.  Every field is a constraining equation
173	    that a later proof can rewrite with:
174	
175	    * `momentum_q_sq` — vector momentum conservation `ℏω/c · k̂ = p⃗ + q⃗`,
176	      eliminated to the cosine-law component statement
177	      `‖q‖² = (ℏω/c)² + ‖p‖² − 2 (ℏω/c) ‖p‖ cos θ`;
178	    * `q_unique` — the vector equation determines `q` uniquely as
179	      `q = (ℏω/c) • k̂ − p`;
180	    * `angle_readout` — the Figure-1c readout that `θ` is the angle between
181	      `p⃗` and the incident photon direction;
182	    * `energy_balance` — non-relativistic energy conservation
183	      `ℏω = ΔU + ‖p‖²/(2·2m) + ‖q‖²/(2m)`.
184	
185	    None of the fields quantifies over configurations or mentions the
186	    minimum; those appear only on the conclusion side of the theorems below. -/
187	structure IsTwoBodyDissociation
188	    (k : PhotonLine) (ω θ m dU : ℝ) (p q : ReactionPlane) : Prop where
189	  /-- Cosine-law magnitude equation from `ℏω/c · k̂ = p⃗ + q⃗`:
190	      `‖q‖² = (ℏω/c)² + ‖p‖² − 2 (ℏω/c) ‖p‖ cos θ`. -/
191	  momentum_q_sq :
192	    ‖q‖ ^ 2 = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) ^ 2 + ‖p‖ ^ 2
193	      - 2 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ
194	  /-- The vector momentum balance determines the `O` momentum uniquely as
195	      `q = (ℏω/c) • k̂ − p`. -/
196	  q_unique : q = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) • k.direction - p
197	  /-- Figure-1c angle readout between the photon direction and `p`. -/
198	  angle_readout : IsScatteringAngle k p θ
199	  /-- Non-relativistic energy balance: the photon energy `ℏω` covers the
200	      dissociation gap `ΔU` plus the classical kinetic energies of the `O₂`
201	      fragment (mass `2m`) and the `O` fragment (mass `m`). -/
202	  energy_balance :
203	    hbar * ω = dU + ‖p‖ ^ 2 / (2 * (2 * m)) + ‖q‖ ^ 2 / (2 * m)
204	
205	/-- Elimination/bridge lemma: the cosine-law component equation is a genuine
206	    consequence of the vector momentum balance and the angle readout, so the
207	    `momentum_q_sq` field is the eliminated shadow of `q_unique` rather than
208	    an independent modelling assumption.  Recording this implication is what
209	    makes the interface constraining: any countermodel must satisfy a vector
210	    equation, not just an isolated scalar identity. -/
211	theorem momentum_q_sq_of_vector_balance
212	    (k : PhotonLine) (ω θ : ℝ) (p q : ReactionPlane)
213	    (hq : q = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) • k.direction - p)
214	    (hθ : IsScatteringAngle k p θ) :
215	    ‖q‖ ^ 2 = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) ^ 2 + ‖p‖ ^ 2
216	      - 2 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := by
217	  have hinner : @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction p = ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := hθ
218	  set a : ℝ := hbar * ω / speedOfLight with ha
219	  have hk : @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction k.direction = 1 := by
220	    rw [@inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, k.direction_unit]
221	    norm_num
222	  have hsq : ‖q‖ ^ 2 = @inner ℝ _ _ q q := by
223	    rw [@inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K]
224	    norm_num
225	  calc ‖q‖ ^ 2 = @inner ℝ _ _ q q := hsq
226	    _ = @inner ℝ _ _ (a • k.direction) (a • k.direction)
227	          - 2 * @inner ℝ _ _ (a • k.direction) p + @inner ℝ _ _ p p := by
228	          rw [hq, real_inner_sub_sub_self]
229	    _ = a ^ 2 * @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction k.direction
230	          - 2 * a * @inner ℝ _ _ k.direction p + @inner ℝ _ _ p p := by
231	          rw [@real_inner_smul_left, @real_inner_smul_left,
232	            @real_inner_smul_right]
233	          ring
234	    _ = a ^ 2 + ‖p‖ ^ 2 - 2 * a * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := by
235	          rw [hk, hinner, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
236	          ring
237	    _ = (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) ^ 2 + ‖p‖ ^ 2
238	          - 2 * (hbar * ω / speedOfLight) * ‖p‖ * Real.cos θ := by
239	          rw [ha]
240	
241	end GoverningLaws

249	minimality statements over lawful configurations, and the candidate formula

266	    no strictly smaller positive frequency is reachable.  This is a

268	    the threshold is left completely open. -/

271	    ∀ ω : ℝ, 0 < ω → ω < ω₀ → ¬ ReachableFrequency m dU θ ω

273	/-- The candidate closed-form forward-branch threshold, in terms of the
274	    oxygen-atom mass `m`, the speed of light `c`, the dissociation gap `ΔU`,
275	    and the scattering angle `θ`:
276	
277	    `Ω(m, c, ΔU, θ) = 3 m c² (1 − √(1 − (2 ΔU/(3 m c²)) (2 sin²θ + 1)))
278	                      / (ℏ (2 sin²θ + 1))`.

280	    This is only a bare real-valued expression — the recorded official
281	    answer.  By itself it asserts nothing about the dissociation; the

283	    the content of `minimum_angular_frequency_T1_C1` below.  The official

296	    2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 + 1 = 2 - Real.cos (2 * θ) := by
297	  have h : Real.cos (2 * θ) = 2 * Real.cos θ ^ 2 - 1 := Real.cos_two_mul θ

307	    here (rather than only the displayed closed form) keeps the official
308	    derivation route — minimization of the energy/momentum balance reduces to
309	    this quadratic — available to later proof steps. -/
310	theorem quadratic_characterization_of_threshold
311	    (m c dU θ : ℝ)
312	    (hm : 0 < m) (hc : 0 < c) (hdU : 0 < dU) (hb : 0 < hbar)
313	    (hθ : IsForwardBranch θ) (hθpos : 0 < θ)
314	    (hfac : (2:ℝ) - Real.cos (2 * θ) ≠ 0)
315	    (hdisc : 0 ≤ 1 - (2 * dU / (3 * m * c ^ 2)) * (2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 + 1)) :

319	      ∀ E : ℝ, 0 < E →
320	        (2 - Real.cos (2 * θ)) * E ^ 2 - 6 * m * c ^ 2 * E + 6 * dU * m * c ^ 2 = 0 →
321	        E₀ ≤ E := by
322	  show 0 < hbar * hbarOmegaMin m c dU θ ∧ _ ∧ _
323	  have hmc : (0:ℝ) < 3 * m * c ^ 2 := by positivity
324	  have hmcne : (3:ℝ) * m * c ^ 2 ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hmc
325	  set S : ℝ := 2 * Real.sin θ ^ 2 + 1 with hSdef
326	  have hS : (1:ℝ) ≤ S := by
327	    rw [hSdef]
328	    have hss := sq_nonneg (Real.sin θ)
329	    linarith
330	  have hSpos : (0:ℝ) < S := lt_of_lt_of_le one_pos hS
331	  have hSne : S ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt hSpos
332	  set D : ℝ := 1 - (2 * dU / (3 * m * c ^ 2)) * S with hDdef

339	    linear_combination (3 * m * c ^ 2) * hs_sq - S * hfracS

341	  have hDlt : (0:ℝ) < 1 - D := by

344	    linarith

352	  have hfac_S : (2:ℝ) - Real.cos (2 * θ) = S := (two_sin_sq_add_one_eq θ).symm

354	  have hΩ : hbarOmegaMin m c dU θ = X / (hbar * S) := rfl
355	  have hE : hbar * hbarOmegaMin m c dU θ = X / S := by
356	    rw [hΩ]

358	    have hden : hbar * S ≠ 0 := mul_ne_zero hbne hSne

361	  · rw [hE]
362	    exact div_pos (mul_pos hmc hone_sub) hSpos
363	  · rw [hfac_S, hE]

481	theorem minimum_angular_frequency_T1_C1
482	    (reg : ConstantRegime) (θ : ℝ)
483	    (hrange : IsAngularRange θ) (hfwd : IsForwardBranch θ) (hθpos : 0 < θ)
484	    (hdisc : 0 ≤ 1 - (2 * dissociationEnergyGap /

489	  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
490	  · -- REACHABILITY — true post-redraft, left to the proof lane.  At

/-- The standard real/complex Euclidean space, functions on a finite type. For an `n`-dimensional
space use `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 (Fin n)`.

For the case when `n = Fin _`, there is `!₂[x, y, ...]` notation for building elements of this type,
analogous to `![x, y, ...]` notation. -/

  PiLp 2 fun _ : n => 𝕜

section Notation
open Lean Meta Elab Term Macro TSyntax PrettyPrinter.Delaborator SubExpr
open Mathlib.Tactic (subscriptTerm)

/-- Notation for vectors in Lp space. `!₂[x, y, ...]` is a shorthand for
`WithLp.toLp 2 ![x, y, ...]`, of type `EuclideanSpace _ (Fin _)`.

This also works for other subscripts. -/
syntax (name := PiLp.vecNotation) "!" noWs subscriptTerm noWs "[" term,* "]" : term
macro_rules | `(!$p:subscript[$e:term,*]) => do
  -- override the `Fin n.succ` to a literal
  let n := e.getElems.size
  `(WithLp.toLp $p (V := ∀ _ : Fin $(quote n), _) ![$e,*])

/-- Unexpander for the `!₂[x, y, ...]` notation. -/
@[app_delab WithLp.toLp]
meta def EuclideanSpace.delabVecNotation : Delab :=
  whenNotPPOption getPPExplicit <| whenPPOption getPPNotation <| withOverApp 3 do
    -- check that the `WithLp.toLp _` is present
    let p : Term ← withNaryArg 0 <| delab
    -- to be conservative, only allow subscripts which are numerals
    guard <| p matches `($_:num)
